_notes:
FROZEN fixture gold set for the retrieval CI gate. Deliberately NOT the native gold set over docs/low-level-design: that corpus IS the haystack, so any PR touching a design doc would shift corpus_sha256 and fail the gate for an unrelated reason. This fixture also ships to CE, where bench/native-goldset.json is excluded as IP.

Twelve documents in six deliberately CROWDED pairs — every question's keywords match at least one sibling — so retrieval must discriminate rather than keyword-match, and a ranking change is observable.

The gate's blocking check (verify-determinism) needs no gold answers at all: it compares what two runs RETRIEVED. gold_document_ids are carried anyway so the same fixture can serve a tier-2 baseline check later without being re-authored, and gold_answer is empty because nothing here judges.

FIXTURE AUTHORING GOTCHA, learned by getting both wrong on 2026-08-12: the field is gold_documents (NOT gold_document_ids), and each entry is the corpus FILENAME INCLUDING .md, because Native.loadCorpus sets DocumentID to e.Name(). Getting either wrong yields gold_documents: null in the artifacts and 'scored: 0' with all metrics at 0 — which reads like broken retrieval and is actually missing labels. The harness is right to refuse rather than score: ContextRecall returns NaN for an unlabelled item precisely so the two cannot be confused.

questions.question: Why did a daemon restart lose chunks that were waiting to be embedded?
What happens to a chunk that cannot be embedded after several retries?
Why could two identical searches return results in a different order while every metric said they matched?
Why are the keyword and semantic arms combined by rank instead of by score?
Why was semantic search silently keyword-only on one embedding transport?
What does the reranker do when it times out?
Why did clearing a cached vector by content hash alone fail to evict anything?
Why can a model with a different native vector width not simply be truncated to fit the schema?
How is a chunk's stored text distinguished from what actually gets embedded?
Which timestamp do temporal filters use, and which one should they use?
